cases.name: Poseidon Wave Media LLC v. Suno, Inc.
UMG Recordings, Sony Music et al. v. Suno, Inc.

profile_text.body:
Suno is a for-profit startup founded in 2022 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Its site describes it as an AI music generator that builds complete songs, including vocals, lyrics, and production, from a text prompt in under a minute, and says Suno Studio is a web-based generative audio workstation that combines traditional DAW functionality with AI-powered music creation. The company describes itself as the market-leading AI song generator and says millions of people use it to make music for fun, for content, and for professional projects.

The site says the free tier is free forever, while paid plans add capacity and rights. The Pro plan is listed at 500 songs a month with royalty free music, access to v5.5, commercial use rights, priority generation, the Song Editor, stem separation into vocal and instrument stems, and audio uploads of up to 8 minutes. The Premier plan is listed at 2,000 songs a month and adds Suno Studio, a multitrack editor, MIDI export, Persona Voices, and early access to new features.

Suno is tracked as a product in the Voice and Audio category, noted for music generation with IP provenance relevance. Eight lawsuits naming Suno appear in the record: Gawronski v. Suno Inc. in the District Court, S.D. Texas; Rugnetta v. Suno, Inc., Pilavian v. Suno, Inc., Reyna v. Suno, and S.A. Jamendo v. Suno Inc. in the District Court, D. Massachusetts; Poseidon Wave Media LLC v. Suno, Inc. in the District Court, S.D. New York; Woulard v. Suno, Inc. in the District Court, N.D. Illinois; and UMG Recordings, Sony Music et al. v. Suno, Inc. in the U.S. District Court, D. Massachusetts. Massachusetts accounts for the largest share of that exposure, at 143 cases.
